checks.fact: Most registered titles show general boundaries.
General-boundary registration does not determine the precise legal line.
No standard tolerance applies between a mapped general boundary and the legal boundary.
No standard measurement applies between a mapped general boundary and the legal boundary.
No standard ratio applies between a mapped general boundary and the legal boundary.
Precise recording depends on survey accuracy.
Large-scale Ordnance Survey mapping is subject to survey tolerances.
A mapped feature indicates a feature existed at the surveyed position subject to mapping limitations.
Physical boundary features can change over time.
Legal-boundary interpretation depends on the relevant conveyance or transfer as a whole.
Extrinsic evidence may be relevant when the plan is insufficiently clear.
General-boundary red edging must not be treated as a surveyed exact legal line.
A determined-boundary route exists when greater precision is required.
A boundary agreement is distinct from a determined-boundary application.

promotion_rule: Exact revision 14 runtime output plus remote integrity readback is required before promoting any parcel height-difference value.
